author: Tatum Peregrin
title: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) Holdings Trimmed by World Asset Management Inc
text:
Posted by Tatum Peregrin on May 5th, 2018 // No Comments
World Asset Management Inc reduced its stake in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 7.4% in the fourth quarter, according to the company in its most recent 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The fund owned 474,685 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 38,085 shares during the quarter. Apple comprises approximately 2.7% of World Asset Management Inc’s holdings, making the stock its largest position. World Asset Management Inc’s holdings in Apple were worth $80,331,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Other large investors have also added to or reduced their stakes in the company. McAdam LLC lifted its holdings in shares of Apple by 8.7% during the second quarter. McAdam LLC now owns 3,609 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $520,000 after purchasing an additional 288 shares during the last quarter. Capital Insight Partners LLC lifted its holdings in shares of Apple by 4.9% during the fourth quarter. Capital Insight Partners LLC now owns 6,292 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $1,065,000 after purchasing an additional 293 shares during the last quarter. Corundum Group Inc. lifted its holdings in shares of Apple by 15.4% during the third quarter. Corundum Group Inc. now owns 2,242 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $346,000 after purchasing an additional 299 shares during the last quarter. Crossvault Capital Management LLC lifted its holdings in shares of Apple by 0.5% during the third quarter. Crossvault Capital Management LLC now owns 65,678 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $10,122,000 after purchasing an additional 300 shares during the last quarter. Finally, Welch Investments LLC lifted its holdings in shares of Apple by 18.7% during the third quarter. Welch Investments LLC now owns 1,907 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $294,000 after purchasing an additional 300 shares during the last quarter. 61.18% of the stock is owned by institutional investors. Shares of Apple stock traded up $6.94 on Friday, hitting $183.83. The stock had a trading volume of 56,123,520 shares, compared to its average volume of 36,848,520. Apple has a twelve month low of $142.20 and a twelve month high of $184.20. The company has a current ratio of 1.46, a quick ratio of 1.20 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80. The company has a market capitalization of $895,918.56, a price-to-earnings ratio of 19.96, a PEG ratio of 1.35 and a beta of 1.26.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last posted its earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 EPS for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. The company had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to the consensus estimate of $60.94 billion. During the same quarter in the prior year, the business earned $2.10 earnings per share. The firm’s revenue for the quarter was up 15.6% on a year-over-year basis. equities research analysts predict that Apple will post 11.28 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
The company also recently announced a quarterly dividend, which will be paid on Thursday, May 17th. Stockholders of record on Monday, May 14th will be given a $0.73 dividend. This is an increase from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. The ex-dividend date is Friday, May 11th. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a dividend yield of 1.59%. Apple’s dividend payout ratio is presently 27.36%.
Apple announced that its Board of Directors has initiated a stock repurchase plan on Tuesday, May 1st that authorizes the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in shares. This repurchase authorization authorizes the iPhone maker to purchase up to 11.9% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock repurchase plans are typically an indication that the company’s management believes its stock is undervalued.
Several research analysts recently weighed in on the company. Atlantic Securities reissued a “neutral” rating and set a $185.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research report on Wednesday. DZ Bank reissued a “buy” rating on shares of Apple in a research report on Thursday. Citigroup reissued a “focus list” rating and set a $142.20 price target (up from $100.00) on shares of Apple in a research report on Wednesday. Zacks Investment Research raised Apple from a “sell” rating to a “hold” rating in a research report on Thursday. Finally, Canaccord Genuity upped their target price on Apple from $200.00 to $208.00 and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Wednesday. One investment analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have issued a hold rating, thirty-three have issued a buy rating and two have given a strong buy rating to the stock. Apple currently has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $204.00.
In related news, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Tuesday, April 3rd. The stock was sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total value of $11,564,692.22. The sale was disclosed in a legal filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which can be accessed through the SEC website . Also, insider Luca Maestri sold 39,122 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, April 13th. The shares were sold at an average price of $174.66, for a total value of $6,833,048.52. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now owns 64,475 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $11,261,203.50. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders sold 125,988 shares of company stock worth $21,336,201 in the last ninety days. 0.08% of the stock is owned by company insiders.
